question_text:
121. Study the following statements :
(a) The Scarecrow gathered nuts as the tree was full of them.
(b) He feared for his life so he got busy in gathering nuts.

122. Study the following statements :
(a) Dorothy was obliged to the Scarecrow.
(b) The Scarecrow vanquished his hunger with nuts.
(c) He gathered so many nuts that no one would remain hungry.
option_a: (a) and (b) are wrong but (c) is right.
option_b: (b) and (c) are wrong but (a) is right.
option_c: (c) and (a) are wrong but (b) is right.
option_d: (a) and (b) are right but (c) is wrong.

question_text:

(4) Adverb

(1) Preposition

125. Which one of the following statements is not true ?
(1) Scarecrow was afraid that the Lion might kill him.
(2) Lion could not eat the nuts gathered by the Scarecrow.
(3) He decided to hunt his prey.
(4) Dorothy felt amused at the way Scarecrow gathered the nuts.
option_a: Scarecrow was afraid that the Lion might kill him.
option_b: Lion could not eat the nuts gathered by the Scarecrow.
option_c: He decided to hunt his prey.
option_d: Dorothy felt amused at the way Scarecrow gathered the nuts.

question_text:

(1) dizzy
(2) messy
(3) cosy
(4) sordid

127. Which one of the following statements is true ?
(1) Scarecrow is not caring.
(2) He knows that the nuts are good for Dorothy.
(3) He shelled the nuts for Dorothy.
(4) Nuts mostly grow on bushes.
option_b: He knows that the nuts are good for Dorothy.
option_c: He shelled the nuts for Dorothy.

question_text:
128. Which of the following statements is/are true ?
(1) The Scarecrow was kind-hearted as he filled the basket with nuts.
(2) He helped Dorothy to keep warm at night.
(3) He kept the Lion away from Dorothy.
(4) Both (1) and (2).
option_a: The Scarecrow was kind-hearted as he filled the basket with nuts.
option_b: He helped Dorothy to keep warm at night.
option_c: He kept the Lion away from Dorothy.

question_text:
129. Why should a birder have sharp ears ?
(1) One can easily distinguish their mating calls.
(2) The birds greet each other with their morning calls.
(3) One can easily locate them from their chirping.
(4) Their shrill shrieking can tell one that they are in danger.
option_a: One can easily distinguish their mating calls.
option_b: The birds greet each other with their morning calls.
option_c: One can easily locate them from their chirping.
option_d: Their shrill shrieking can tell one that they are in danger.

question_text:
130. Study the following statements :
(a) Different chirpings of birds evoke different emotions in a birder.
(b) Sometimes birds make their nests hidden from public view.
(1) (a) is right and (b) is wrong.
(2) (b) is right and (a) is wrong.
(3) Both (a) and (b) are right.
(4) Both (a) and (b) are wrong.

131. Study the following statements :
(a) The writer approves of the conduct of Delhi people.
(b) Indian mynas are generally known for their noisy quarrels.
(c) A myna couple can also be found enjoying themselves.
(1) (a) and (b) are right but (c) is wrong.
(2) (b) and (c) are right but (a) is wrong.
(3) (a) and (c) are right but (b) is wrong.
(4) (a) and (b) are wrong but (c) is right.
option_a: (a) and (b) are right but (c) is wrong.
option_b: (b) and (c) are right but (a) is wrong.
option_c: (a) and (c) are right but (b) is wrong.
option_d: (a) and (b) are wrong but (c) is right.

136. Assessment tools and processes at the foundation stage should be designed in a way that :
(1) explicit tests and examinations become appropriate for learners.
(2) they become a natural extension of the child's learning experience.
(3) learner's progress is described and analysed with that of the overall class performance.
(4) a teacher may use common single method to assess the achievement of all the learners.
option_a: explicit tests and examinations become appropriate for learners.
option_b: they become a natural extension of the child's learning experience.
option_c: learner's progress is described and analysed with that of the overall class performance.
option_d: a teacher may use common single method to assess the achievement of all the learners.

question_text:
137. Children's cognitive development and language :
(1) is related to the principle of linking stimulus-response and a process of imitation.
(2) is that an individual is born with a tool to master the language.
(3) development bear no relationship.
(4) is closely related to the culture and the community in which children live.
option_a: is related to the principle of linking stimulus-response and a process of imitation.
option_b: is that an individual is born with a tool to master the language.
option_d: is closely related to the culture and the community in which children live.

question_text:
138. One of the best way to learn a second language is :
(1) being in a classroom where you can focus on the grammar and receive help from a teacher.
(2) by constant contact with native speakers in their own society.
(3) by repeating and practicing the dialogues as done in the audio-lingual method.
(4) by joining a speaking course for the target language.
option_a: being in a classroom where you can focus on the grammar and receive help from a teacher.
option_b: by constant contact with native speakers in their own society.
option_c: by repeating and practicing the dialogues as done in the audio-lingual method.
option_d: by joining a speaking course for the target language.

question_text:
139. "Language learning is an intensive process that begins at birth and continues throughtout life."
Do you agree or disagree with the above statement ?
(1) I agree with this statement.
(2) I disagree with this statement.
(3) I partially agree with the statement.
(4) I partially disagree with the statement.
option_c: I partially agree with the statement.
option_d: I partially disagree with the statement.

question_text:
140. Along with print books and audio books the books that engage the tactile abilities of young children should be a part of the classroom because :
(1) it brings variety to the class and children love variety.
(2) it gives autonomy to teachers to use different books for assessment.
(3) it makes books more accessible to diverse learners.
(4) these books will not overly burden a teacher.
option_a: it brings variety to the class and children love variety.
option_b: it gives autonomy to teachers to use different books for assessment.
option_c: it makes books more accessible to diverse learners.
option_d: these books will not overly burden a teacher.

question_text:
141. A teacher asked the students of class V to read the story quickly and then put the four pictures in order. The purpose of this activity is to :
(1) arrange the picture cards.
(2) give them practice to reading for the gist.
(3) give them practice in reading for specific information.
(4) revise the new and difficult vocabulary of the story.
option_b: give them practice to reading for the gist.
option_c: give them practice in reading for specific information.
option_d: revise the new and difficult vocabulary of the story.

question_text:
142. This reading has certain learning aims and tasks, learners are supposed to read the text in detail with concentration and due care, It is called :
(1) Extensive reading
(2) Intensive reading
(3) Guided reading
(4) Pleasure reading

143. The students learn patterns of language by repeating model sentences that the teacher provides. They memorise set phrases and receive positive reinforcement from their teacher when they perform the drills correctly. The teacher is using the :
(1) Audio-lingual method
(2) Communicative approach
(3) Total physical response
(4) Structural approach

144. Learners are memorising grammar rules and vocabulary and large amount of work is done in their mother tongue. Which method is being used by the teacher into his language class ?
(1) Direct method
(2) Natural approach
(3) Communicative teaching
(4) Grammar Translation

145. If children hear two languages spoken around them, this exposure will :
(1) put the children at a disadvantage.
(2) put the children at an advantage.
(3) not make any difference to the children.
(4) confuse the children, hindering understanding.
option_a: put the children at a disadvantage.
option_b: put the children at an advantage.
option_c: not make any difference to the children.

question_text:
146. A big challenge in learning to read is finding motivation and good children's literature. To overcome this challenge :
(1) Teachers should motivate them to read a book everyday as homework.
(2) Encourage parents to establish a small library at home.
(3) Provide easily accessible Children's literature to motivate and generate interest in reading.
(4) School authorities must take learners to book fairs to generate motivation and interest in reading books.
option_a: Teachers should motivate them to read a book everyday as homework.
option_b: Encourage parents to establish a small library at home.
option_c: Provide easily accessible Children's literature to motivate and generate interest in reading.
option_d: School authorities must take learners to book fairs to generate motivation and interest in reading books.

147. To assess reading skills at primary level a language teacher should most importantly focus on :
(1) identifying the letters of alphabet.
(2) use of punctuation mark.
(3) reading at a proper speed.
(4) reading with understanding.

148. A good speaking activity is the one during which :
(1) teachers explains more
(2) learners listens more
(3) learners talk more
